rounds.text: Viceroy Hotels Ltd demonstrates strong top-line momentum, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 39% [E17] and a 5-year compounded sales growth of 33% [E15], alongside screen triggers noting sales up year-over-year by 56% [E61]. Profitability is compounding impressively over medium and long horizons, showing 22% annualized profit growth over 5 years [E19] and a 617% surge over 3 years [E20], supported by a healthy 22.4% CAGR over the last 5 years [E56]. Operating margins have expanded substantially by 15 percentage points in the TTM period to reach 28% [E27], while cash generation remains exceptionally solid with a 3.22x cash conversion rate and ₹58 Cr in operating cash flow for March 2026 [E31, E32]. Operational efficiency is further signaled by a 71.9% reduction in capital-work-in-progress to ₹16 Cr, indicating that major capital expenditures are largely complete and new capacity is primed to come online [E37]. Market participation is robust, with the stock trading near its highs at 82% of its 52-week range [E44], positioned above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E46], and boasting a high relative-strength rating of 88 against the Nifty 500 [E47]. Conceded: [E41, E42, E43, E68].

Viceroy Hotels Ltd carries an aggressive valuation that is unsupported by its underlying fundamentals and returns profile, trading at an exorbitant P/E of 55.2x against a sector benchmark of 22.91x and an EV/EBITDA of 23.26x versus the sector's 11.51x [E1, E6, E11]. This rich multiple leaves no margin of safety, as a discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value at Rs 111 per share against a market price of Rs 148, resulting in a -33.1% margin of safety and a reverse DCF implying an unrealistic 22.0% earnings growth [E1, E2, E41, E42, E43]. Furthermore, the company's profitability metrics drastically lag sector benchmarks, with an ROE of 5.49% against 7.06% and an ROCE of 5.69% against 7.96%, compounded by a severe negative free cash flow of Rs -65 Cr in March 2026 despite strong reported operating cash flow [E8, E9, E10, E32, E33]. Insider conviction is also notably deteriorating, evidenced by promoters slashing their holding from 95.00% in December 2023 down to 74.03% in September 2026, alongside domestic institutions cutting stakes to a meager 0.34% [E38, E39]. Compounded historical sales growth over a 10-year span sits at an anemic 1%, and the quarterly operating-margin trend has been decreasing over the last four quarters while net profit dropped 49% year-on-year [E14, E30, E65]. Conceded: the company has delivered strong profit growth of 22.4% CAGR over the last 5 years alongside a recent TTM sales increase of 39% and an operating margin reaching 28% [E17, E27, E56].

While the bear points to an expensive headline P/E of 55.2x and high EV/EBITDA, this multiple is backed by explosive recent catalysts, including a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 39% and a 5-year profit CAGR of 22.4% that outpaces the sector median profit growth of 21.1% [E1, E6, E11, E17, E56, E71]. Furthermore, the bear's focus on historical 10-year sales ignores the accelerating near-term inflection where 5-year sales growth reaches 33% and quarterly results are expected to be good [E14, E15, E55]. Conceded: free cash flow was negative at Rs -65 Cr in March 2026, but overall operating cash flow hit a strong Rs 58 Cr and capital-expenditure overhang has largely cleared with CWIP dropping 71.9% to free up future capacity [E32, E33, E37]. Finally, the technical reality completely defies the bear's narrative of weakness, as the stock trades above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a stellar relative-strength rating of 88 against the Nifty 500 [E46, E47].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales growth reached 39% and 5-year profit CAGR is 22.4%, which slightly edges out the sector median profit growth of 21.1% [E17, E56, E71]. However, the bull's attempt to justify a 55.2x P/E and a 23.26x EV/EBITDA using these growth metrics ignores how severely they lag behind expectations baked into the share price [E1, E6, E11]. The stock's price-led growth—where price gains have outpaced profit growth by 19% recently—demonstrates that expectations are running well ahead of actual delivery [E53]. Furthermore, relying on positive near-term expectations and a drop in capital work-in-progress to excuse negative free cash flow of Rs -65 Cr ignores the severe fundamental drag of a low 5.49% ROE and 5.69% ROCE, both of which trail sector benchmarks significantly [E9, E10, E33, E37, E55]. Finally, a strong relative strength rating of 88 and trading above moving averages do not eliminate valuation risk, given that the reverse DCF indicates the current price already demands an unrealistic 22.0% earnings growth rate [E43, E46, E47].
